paragraphs: Mueller Water Products, Inc. ("Mueller," "we," "our," or the "Company") is a leading manufacturer and marketer of products and solutions used in the transmission, distribution and measurement of water in North America. Our products and solutions are used by municipalities and the residential and non-residential construction industries. Some of our products have leading positions as a result of their strong brand recognition and reputation for quality, service and innovation. We believe we have one of the largest installed bases of iron gate valves and fire hydrants in the United States. Our iron gate valve and hydrant products are specified for use in the largest 100 metropolitan areas in the United States. Our large installed base, broad product range and well-known brands have led to long-standing relationships with the key distributors and end users of our products. Our consolidated net sales were $1,429.7 million in 2025.

We operate our business through two segments, Water Flow Solutions and Water Management Solutions. Segment sales, operating results and additional financial data and commentary are provided in the Segment Analysis section in Part II, Item 7. "MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS" and in Note 14. of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8. "FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTARY DATA" of this Annual Report.

In January 2025, we announced the appointment of Ms. Melissa Rasmussen as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer effective March 3, 2025. On March 1, 2025, Mr. Steven S. Heinrichs transitioned from his roles as Chief Financial Officer and Chief Legal Officer to Senior Advisor and remained an advisor until September 30, 2025. In August 2025, we announced the appointment of Ms. Richelle R. Feyerherm as Chief Accounting Officer effective August 15, 2025. Ms. Feyerherm also serves as the Company's principal accounting officer. On November 6, 2025, we announced that Ms. Marietta Edmunds Zakas will retire as the Company's Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Company's Board of Directors, effective as of February 9, 2026 (the "Transition Date"). In connection with Ms. Zakas' retirement, the Company's Board of Directors appointed Mr. Paul McAndrew as President and Chief Executive Officer, effective as of the Transition Date.

The Water Flow Solutions product portfolio includes iron gate valves, specialty valves and service brass products. Net sales of products in the Water Flow Solutions business unit were approximately 58% of fiscal 2025 consolidated net sales.

The Water Management Solutions product and service portfolio includes fire hydrants, repair and installation, natural gas, metering, leak detection, as well as pressure management and control products and solutions. Net sales of products and services in the Water Management Solutions business unit were approximately 42% of fiscal 2025 consolidated net sales.
Our business strategy is to capitalize on the large, attractive and growing water infrastructure markets worldwide. Key elements of this strategy are as follows:

We expect to make disciplined investments in our commercial and operational capabilities to drive additional performance improvements. We are focused on improving operational excellence, increasing supply chain efficiencies and developing advanced manufacturing capabilities to drive productivity and increase domestic capacity across our facilities. We expect these efforts will drive sales growth, improve product margins, and facilitate innovation and new product development. Productivity improvements within our facilities are expected to drive cost reductions to support additional manufacturing initiatives and ongoing investment in product development.

Since 2018, we have prioritized capital investments to modernize our manufacturing facilities and processes, expand capacity and capabilities for domestic manufacturing and accelerate new product development. We believe these investments will drive margin expansion by lowering costs, expanding our product portfolio, and improving product quality. Our new brass foundry in Decatur, Illinois, is operational, and we have closed our legacy brass foundry, which was built in the early 1900s. We expect these investments to support our domestic manufacturing capabilities for specialty and large valves and to capitalize

on the growing need for highly engineered valves required for water infrastructure projects. Additionally, we expect these investments to drive operational efficiencies, expand capabilities for American-made products, advance our sustainability initiatives, and help accelerate product development.

We plan to continue to invest in process improvements to support our objective of being the preferred partner for our customers. We are making disciplined investments in our commercial teams to enhance our customer experience to further differentiate us in the market and support our opportunities for net sales growth. Expanding our systems and employee capabilities will allow us to improve our customer experience. We continue to invest time and resources to deepen our channel partnerships and end-customer relationships to increase our presence in the fastest-growing markets. Additionally, we seek to attract and retain customers through product training and engineering resources to ascertain, educate and understand project requirements. We plan to continue to invest in our product development capabilities, including our research and development processes, to develop and market new products and services. We expect to add new products to our portfolio and offer new products in different end markets.

We believe our employees are our greatest asset, and we strive to provide a safe, inclusive, high-performance culture where our people can thrive. We endeavor to recruit, develop, engage, train and protect our workforce. Our core values of respect, integrity, trust, safety and inclusion shape our culture and define who we are. We continue to make investments to enhance collaboration and teamwork throughout the organization to create a culture of talent development, enabling us to execute on our strategic opportunities and make Mueller a preferred place to work. We prioritize employee engagement and transparency by implementing programs and processes to provide our employees with opportunities to ask questions, voice concerns and share feedback. This communication is accomplished in part by conducting employee experience surveys, global town halls and facility employee meetings.

We will continue to evaluate the acquisition of strategic businesses, technologies and product lines that have the potential to strengthen our competitive position, enhance or expand our existing product and service offerings, expand our technological capabilities, leverage our manufacturing capabilities, provide synergistic opportunities, enhance our customer relationships or allow us to enter new markets. As part of this strategy, we have pursued, and may continue to pursue, international opportunities, including acquisitions, joint ventures and partnerships.

We offer a broad line of water infrastructure, and flow control products and services primarily in the United States and Canada. Water Flow Solutions sells iron gate and specialty valves, and service brass products. Water Management Solutions sells fire hydrants, repair and installation, natural gas, metering, leak detection and pressure management and control products and solutions. Our products are designed, manufactured and tested in compliance with relevant industry standards. Our water distribution products are manufactured to meet or exceed American Water Works Association ("AWWA") standards and, where applicable, certified to National Science Foundation ("NSF")/American National Standards Institute ("ANSI") Standard 61 for potable water conveyance. Underwriters Laboratory ("UL") and FM Approvals ("FM"), two third-party certification companies, have approved many of these products. Additionally, our products are typically specified by a water utility for use in its infrastructure system.

Water Flow Solutions' product portfolio includes iron gate valves, specialty valves and service brass products. We recognized $824.9 million, $755.5 million and $634.4 million of net sales in our 2025, 2024 and 2023 fiscal years, respectively, for Water Flow Solutions products and solutions.

headings: Risks related to our industries
A significant portion of our business depends on spending for water and wastewater infrastructure construction activity.
Residential construction activity is important to our business and adverse conditions or sustained uncertainty within this market could adversely affect our financial results.
Our business depends on a small group of key customers for a significant portion of our sales.
Strong competition could adversely affect prices and demand for our products and services, which would adversely affect our operating results and financial condition.
Risks related to our business strategy
We may not be able to adequately manage the risks associated with our products, systems and solutions, including increased warranty costs.
Our products and services may be affected from time to time by design and manufacturing defects that could materially adversely affect the business and result in harm to our reputation.
Potential international business opportunities may expose us to additional risks, including foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations.
Risks related to our operations
Our reliance on vendors for certain products, some of which are single-source or limited-source suppliers, could harm our business by adversely affecting product availability, reliability or cost.
A disruption in our supply chain or other factors impacting the distribution of our products could adversely affect our business.
Seasonal demand for certain of our products and services may adversely affect our financial results.
Transportation costs are relatively high for most of our products.
Our business, financial condition and results of operations may be adversely impacted by the effects of inflation.
Our high fixed costs may make it more difficult for us to respond to economic cycles.
We may experience difficulties implementing upgrades to our software systems.
Normal operations at our key manufacturing facilities may be interrupted.
Any inability to protect our intellectual property or our failure to effectively defend against intellectual property infringement claims could adversely affect our competitive position.
We may fail to effectively manage confidential data, which could harm our reputation, result in substantial additional costs and subject us to litigation.
Cyberattacks and security vulnerabilities could lead to reduced sales, increased costs, liability claims, unauthorized access to customer data or harm to our reputation.
Misuse of our technology-enabled products, services and solutions could lead to reduced sales, increased costs, liability claims or harm to our reputation.
We are subject to a variety of claims, investigations and litigation that could adversely affect our results of operations and harm our reputation.

We are subject to stringent environmental, health and safety laws and regulations that impose significant compliance costs. Any failure to comply with these laws and regulations may adversely affect us.
Climate change and legal or regulatory responses thereto may have an adverse impact on our business and results of operations.
We rely on successors to Tyco to indemnify us for certain liabilities and they may become financially unable or fail to comply with the terms of the indemnity.
Risks related to our human capital

If we are unable to negotiate collective bargaining agreements on satisfactory terms or we experience strikes, work stoppages, labor unrest or higher than normal absenteeism, our business could suffer.
Our expenditures for pension obligations could be materially higher than we have predicted.
Risks related to our international operations
Any failure to satisfy international trade laws and regulations or to otherwise comply with changes or other trade developments may adversely affect us.
The prices of our purchased components and raw materials can be volatile.
Our business, operating results and financial condition may be negatively impacted by geopolitical events, including wars, terrorism, industrial accidents and other business interruptions.
paragraphs: Our primary end markets are repair and replacement of water infrastructure, driven by municipal spending and new water infrastructure installation in connection with new residential construction. As a result, a significant portion of our business depends on local, state and federal spending on water and wastewater infrastructure upgrade, repair and replacement projects. Funds for water and wastewater infrastructure repair and replacement typically come from local taxes, water fees and water rates. State and local governments and private water entities that do not adequately budget for expenditures when setting tax rates, water rates and water fees, as applicable, could be unable to pay for water infrastructure repair and replacement if they do not have access to other funding sources. In addition, reductions or delays in federal spending related to water or wastewater infrastructure could adversely affect state or local projects and thus may adversely affect our financial results.

Governments and private water entities may have limited abilities to increase taxes, water fees or water rates, as applicable. It is not unusual for water and wastewater projects to be delayed and rescheduled for a number of reasons, including changes in project priorities, increasing interest rates, inflation and difficulties in complying with environmental and other governmental regulations. For example, changes in interest rates and credit markets, including municipal bonds, mortgages, home equity loans and consumer credit, have in the past, and may in the future, significantly increase the cost of the projects in which our products are utilized, such as in new residential construction and water and wastewater infrastructure upgrade, repair and replacement projects, and lead to such projects being reduced, delayed and/or rescheduled, which could result in a decrease in our sales and earnings and adversely affect our financial condition. In addition, higher interest rates are often accompanied by inflation. We have in the past, and may in the future, be unable to raise the prices of our products sufficiently to keep up with the rate of inflation, which would reduce our profit margins and cash flows.

Some state and local governments may place significant restrictions on the use of water by their constituents and/or increase their water conservation efforts. These types of water use restrictions and water conservation efforts may lead to reduced water revenues by private water entities, municipalities or other governmental agencies, which could similarly affect funding decisions for water-related projects.

Poor economic conditions may cause states, municipalities or private water entities to receive lower than anticipated revenues, which may lead to reduced or delayed funding for water infrastructure projects. Even if favorable economic conditions exist, water infrastructure owners may choose not to address deferred infrastructure needs as a result of a variety of political factors or competing spending priorities.
Low levels of spending for water and wastewater infrastructure construction activity could adversely affect our sales, profitability and cash flows.

New water and wastewater infrastructure spending is heavily dependent upon residential construction. As a result, our financial performance depends significantly on the stability and growth of the residential construction market. This market depends on a variety of factors beyond our control, including household formation, consumer confidence, interest rates, inflation and the availability of mortgage financing, as well as the mix between single and multifamily construction, availability of construction labor and ultimately the extent to which new construction leads to the development of raw land. Adverse conditions or sustained uncertainty regarding the residential construction market have had, and may in the future have, an adverse effect on our sales, profitability and cash flows, including the risk that one or more of our distributors and/or end use customers decide to delay purchasing, or determine not to purchase, our products or services.

paragraphs: In October 2023, the Israel-Hamas war caused a temporary shutdown in our facility in Ariel, Israel. While we reopened the facility in November 2023, the war caused supply chain challenges that hindered our ability to most efficiently manufacture our products produced in Israel. While the facility was adversely impacted by this event, we have mitigated operational risk by expanding our suppliers and improving throughput in order to increase production levels and to meet customer delivery times. While net sales levels have returned to pre-war levels, margin expansion was further hindered by newly implemented tariffs on products manufactured in Israel and imported into the United States.

While newly implemented tariffs are adversely impacting several product lines, Repair and Specialty Valve product lines are bearing most of the higher costs. In response to tariffs that went into effect in the second half of fiscal 2025, we implemented additional pricing actions, which are expected to mostly offset tariff costs in dollar terms but will result in tariff-related impacts being dilutive to margins. As the tariffs remain uncertain and volatile, we will continue to monitor the situation and take appropriate actions to address inflationary and other cost pressures.

At the end of the first quarter, we ceased melting and casting operations at our legacy brass foundry and transitioned production to our state-of-the-art foundry. We expect this transition will improve operational efficiency and enable us to better serve our service brass customers. As part of Mueller's overall strategy, we will continue investing in our foundries to expand

capacity, increase manufacturing efficiencies and strategically position ourselves as the demand for domestic product is expected to increase given the uncertainty in the current geopolitical and tariff environment.

For fiscal year 2026, we anticipate that consolidated net sales will increase between 1.4% and 2.8% as compared with fiscal 2025. The external operating environment remains uncertain as we face changes in government policies, including possible disruptions to global supply chains resulting from such changes, the interest rate and tariff environment, as well as geopolitical conditions and labor and material inflation and availability. We expect these challenges to continue into fiscal 2026. We continue to anticipate resilient demand associated with the municipal repair and replacement end market driven by the aging water infrastructure and increasing water rates, moderated by budgetary and operational pressures on municipalities. We anticipate that new residential construction activity and new lot and land development will be relatively constrained by the uncertainty in the economy, affordability concerns and interest rate environment, depending on the geographic region.

Our orders and shipments in 2025 reflected a more typical operating environment compared with the high backlog environment we experienced during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. For fiscal 2026, we assume that we will continue to experience a more normalized operating environment leading to normalized seasonality for consolidated net sales. Therefore, we anticipate quarterly consolidated net sales as a percentage of fiscal year 2026 consolidated net sales to be the highest in the third quarter and lowest in the first quarter, with a sequential increase in consolidated net sales in the second quarter as the construction season ramps up for the Spring. For fiscal 2026, we anticipate that inflation will continue to modestly impact manufacturing costs, primarily due to wage inflation, as well as raw materials and purchased parts. In addition, higher direct tariff costs of approximately 3% of costs of goods sold are expected to continue to contribute to inflationary pressures in 2026. While pricing actions were taken in 2025 in response to new tariffs, we will continue to monitor the market and economic conditions impacting our business and take appropriate actions to address inflationary and other cost pressures by implementing price increases, cost containment measures and supplier management measures, among other actions.

paragraphs: Mueller Water Products, Inc. ("Mueller," "we," "our," 或 the "Company") 為北美地區水傳輸、分配與測量所使用產品與解決方案的主要製造與行銷廠商。我們的產品與解決方案被各級政府與住宅及非住宅建設產業所使用。部分產品因強大的品牌認知度與品質、服務與創新聲譽而具領導地位。我們相信本公司在美國擁有鐵製閥門與消防栓最大的安裝基礎。本公司鐵製閥門與消防栓產品被指定用於美國最大的100個都會區。我們的大型安裝基礎、廣泛的產品範圍與知名的品牌已促成與我們產品主要經銷商與最終用戶之間長期的合作關係。本公司合併後的淨銷售額為2025年14.297億美元。
本公司透過兩個應報告分部運作業務，分別為水流量解決方案與水管理解決方案。各分部銷售、營運成果以及額外的財務資料與評論，請參閱年度報告第二部分第七項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析" 的 "Segment Analysis" 節，以及第二部分第八項 "財務報表與補充資料" 的註釋第14項 "合併財務報表註釋"。

2025年1月，本公司宣佈任命Melissa Rasmussen女士為高級副總裁兼首席財務官，生效日期為2025年3月3日。2025年3月1日，Steven S. Heinrichs先生從首席財務官與首席法律官職務轉任高級顧問，並持續擔任顧問至2025年9月30日。2025年8月，本公司宣佈任命Richelle R. Feyerherm女士為首席會計官，生效日期為2025年8月15日。Feyerherm女士同時擔任本公司主要會計官。2025年11月6日，本公司宣佈Marietta Edmunds Zakas女士將於2026年2月9日（稱為"過渡日"）退休，擔任本公司首席執行官與董事會成員。為配合Zakas女士退休，本公司董事會任命Paul McAndrew先生為總裁與首席執行官，生效日期為過渡日。
水流量解決方案產品組合包括鐵製閥門、專業閥門與服務黃銅產品。水流量解決方案業務單位的產品淨銷售額約為2025會計年度合併後淨銷售額的58%。
水管理解決方案產品與服務組合包括消防栓、維修與安裝、天然氣、測量、洩漏偵測，以及壓力管理與控制產品與解決方案。水管理解決方案業務單位的產品與服務淨銷售額約為2025會計年度合併後淨銷售額的42%。
本公司業務策略為把握全球規模龐大、具吸引力且成長迅速的水基礎設施市場。此策略的主要要素如下：
我們預期會在商業與營運能力上進行有紀律的投資，以推動進一步的績效改善。我們專注於提升營運卓越性、增加供應鏈效率，並發展先進製造能力，以提高生產力並增加各廠區的國內製造能力。我們預期這些努力將推動銷售成長、改善產品毛利率，並促進創新與新產品開發。廠區內的生產力改善預期將推動成本降低，以支持進一步的製造計畫與持續投資於產品開發。
自2018年起，我們已優先進行資本投資，以現代化製造廠區與流程、擴充國內製造能力與能力，並加速新產品開發。我們相信這些投資將透過降低成本、擴充產品組合與改善產品品質，推動毛利率擴張。我們在伊利諾州Decatur的全新黃銅鑄造廠已開始運作，並已關閉建於1900年代初期的舊黃銅鑄造廠。我們預期這些投資將支持我們在專業閥門與大型閥門的國內製造能力，並實現
針對水基礎建設專案所需高工程化閥門之需求持續成長。此外，我們預期這些投資將提升作業效率、擴展美國製產品之能力、推進我們的永續發展計畫，並協助加速產品開發。

我們計畫持續投資於流程改進，以支持我們成為客戶首選合作夥伴之目標。我們對商業團隊進行有紀律的投資，以提升客戶體驗，進一步區隔我們在市場的競爭優勢，並支持我們淨銷售額成長之機會。擴充我們的系統與員工能力，將有助於改善客戶體驗。我們持續投資時間與資源，深化通路夥伴與終端客戶關係，以增加我們在成長最快的市場之存在感。此外，我們計畫透過產品培訓與工程資源吸引並留住客戶，以瞭解、教育並掌握專案需求。我們計畫持續投資於產品開發能力，包括研究與開發流程，以開發與行銷新產品與服務。我們預期將新增產品至我們的產品組合，並在不同終端市場推出新產品。

我們認為員工是我們最重要的資產，我們致力於提供一個安全、包容、高績效的文化環境，讓員工得以發揮所長。我們努力招募、培訓、激勵、訓練與保護我們的員工。我們的核心價值觀，包括尊重、誠信、信任、安全與包容，塑造我們的文化並定義我們的本質。我們持續投資以增強組織內的協作與團隊合作，建立人才發展的文化，使我們得以執行戰略機會，並使Mueller成為員工心目中理想的就業地點。我們優先考量員工參與與透明度，透過實施計畫與流程，讓員工有機會提問、表達意見與提供反饋。此溝通部分透過進行員工體驗問卷、全球董事會與廠區員工會議來達成。
我們將持續評估取得戰略性業務、技術與產品線的機會，這些機會有潛力強化我們的競爭優勢，提升或擴展我們現有的產品與服務，擴充我們的技術能力，善用我們的製造能力，創造協同效益，提升我們的客戶關係，或使我們能夠進入新市場。根據此策略，我們已追求並可能持續追求國際機會，包括收購、合資企業與合作夥伴關係。

我們提供廣泛的水基礎建設與流量控制產品與服務，主要在美國與加拿大。Water Flow Solutions銷售鐵製閥門與特殊閥門，以及服務銅製產品。Water Management Solutions銷售消防栓、維修與安裝、天然氣、計量、漏電偵測與壓力管理與控制產品與解決方案。我們的產品設計、製造與測試均符合相關產業標準。我們的水分佈產品製造符合或超越美國水協會（"American Water Works Association"，簡稱"AWWA"）標準，並在適用範圍內，經認證符合國家科學基金會（"National Science Foundation"，簡稱"NSF"）/美國國家標準協會（"American National Standards Institute"，簡稱"ANSI"）標準61，用於飲用水傳輸。Underwriters Laboratory（"UL"）與FM Approvals（"FM"）為兩家第三方認證機構，已核准許多這些產品。此外，我們的產品通常被水電公司指定用於其基礎設施系統。

paragraphs: 2023年10月，以色列與哈瑪斯的戰爭導致我們位於以色列艾利爾的廠區暫時停工。雖然我們於2023年11月重新開放了該廠區，但戰爭導致供應鏈挑戰，影響我們在以色列製造產品的效率。雖然該廠區受到此事件的負面影響，我們已透過擴大供應商網路與提升產能，以增加生產量並符合客戶交貨時間。雖然淨銷售額已恢復至戰爭前的水平，但新實施的關稅進一步抑制了毛利率的擴張。
雖然新實施的關稅對多個產品線造成負面影響，但修復與特殊閥門產品線承擔了較高的成本。針對2025財年第二季生效的關稅，我們已實施額外的價格調整措施，預期這些措施能在金額上抵消大部分關稅成本，但會對毛利率產生稀釋影響。由於關稅情況仍不確定且波動性高，我們將持續監測此情況，並採取適當措施應對通貨膨脹及其他成本壓力。
在第一季末，我們停止了位於傳統黃銅鑄造廠的熔煉與鑄造作業，並將生產轉移至我們的先進鑄造廠。我們預期此轉移將提高運營效率，並使我們能更好地服務黃銅服務客戶。根據米勒公司的整體戰略，我們將持續投資於鑄造廠，以擴大規模

capacity, increase manufacturing efficiencies and strategically position ourselves as the demand for domestic product is expected to increase given the uncertainty in the current geopolitical and tariff environment.

For fiscal year 2026, we anticipate that consolidated net sales will increase between 1.4% and 2.8% as compared with fiscal 2025. The external operating environment remains uncertain as we face changes in government policies, including possible disruptions to global supply chains resulting from such changes, the interest rate and tariff environment, as well as geopolitical conditions and labor and material inflation and availability. We expect these challenges to continue into fiscal 2026. We continue to anticipate resilient demand associated with the municipal repair and replacement end market driven by the aging water infrastructure and increasing water rates, moderated by budgetary and operational pressures on municipalities. We anticipate that new residential construction activity and new lot and land development will be relatively constrained by the uncertainty in the economy, affordability concerns and interest rate environment, depending on the geographic region.

Our orders and shipments in 2025 reflected a more typical operating environment compared with the high backlog environment we experienced during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. For fiscal 2026, we assume that we will continue to experience a more normalized operating environment leading to normalized seasonality for consolidated net sales. Therefore, we anticipate quarterly consolidated net sales as a percentage of fiscal year 2026 consolidated net sales to be the highest in the third quarter and lowest in the first quarter, with a sequential increase in consolidated net sales in the second quarter as the construction season ramps up for the Spring. For fiscal 2026, we anticipate that inflation will continue to modestly impact manufacturing costs, primarily due to wage inflation, as well as raw materials and purchased parts. In addition, higher direct tariff costs of approximately 3% of costs of goods sold are expected to continue to contribute to inflationary pressures in 2026. While pricing actions were taken in 2025 in response to new tariffs, we will continue to monitor the market and economic conditions impacting our business and take appropriate actions to address inflationary and other cost pressures by implementing price increases, cost containment measures and supplier management measures, among other actions.

headings: 與我們產業相關的風險
我們業務的很大一部分取決於水與污水處理基礎設施建設活動的支出。
住宅建設活動對我們的業務至關重要，若此市場出現不利情況或持續不確定性，可能會對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
我們的業務取決於一小羣關鍵客戶，這些客戶為我們銷售收入的很大一部分。
強烈的競爭可能會對我們產品與服務的價格與需求產生負面影響，進而對我們的營運結果與財務狀況產生負面影響。
與我們業務策略相關的風險
我們可能無法充分管理與我們產品、系統與解決方案相關的風險，包括增加的保固成本。
我們的產品與服務可能會因設計與製造缺陷而偶爾受到影響，這可能會對業務產生重大負面影響，並導致我們聲譽受損。
潛在的國際業務機會可能使我們面臨額外風險，包括外幣匯率波動。
與我們營運相關的風險
我們對某些產品的供應商依賴性，其中一些產品為單一來源或有限來源供應商，可能會透過影響產品可得性、可靠性或成本而損害我們的業務。
我們供應鏈的中斷或其他影響產品分銷的因素，可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
某些產品與服務的季節性需求，可能會對我們的財務結果產生不利影響。
我們大多數產品的運輸成本相對較高。
我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果可能因通貨膨脹的影響而受到不利影響。
我們的高固定成本可能使我們更難以應對經濟週期。
我們可能面臨困難，無法執行我們軟體系統的升級作業。
我們主要製造設施的正常運作可能受到中斷。
任何無法保護我們的智慧財產權，或我們未能有效防範智慧財產權侵權聲索的情況，都可能不利於我們的競爭地位。
我們可能無法有效管理機密資料，這可能會損害我們的聲譽，導致額外的重大成本，並使我們面臨訴訟。
網路攻擊與安全漏洞可能導致銷售減少、成本增加、賠償聲索、未經授權存取客戶資料或損害我們的聲譽。
我們技術驅動的產品、服務與解決方案被誤用，可能導致銷售減少、成本增加、賠償聲索或損害我們的聲譽。
我們面臨多種聲索、調查與訴訟，這可能不利於我們的營運結果，並損害我們的聲譽。
我們受到嚴格的環境、健康與安全法規管制，這些法規會產生顯著的合規成本。任何未能遵守這些法規的情況，都可能對我們造成不利影響。
氣候變遷及相關法律或法規的回應可能對我們的業務及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們依賴取得Tyco繼承權的公司為我們賠償特定負債，而這些公司可能無法負擔財務責任或未能遵守賠償條款。
與我們人力資本相關的風險
若我們無法在滿意的條件下達成集體談判協議，或遭遇罷工、停工、勞資糾紛或高於正常水平的缺勤率，可能對我們的業務造成影響。
我們為退休金義務所支出的費用可能高於我們預測的金額。
與我們國際業務相關的風險
若未能符合國際貿易法律法規或未能因應貿易法規的變更或其他貿易發展，可能對我們產生不利影響。

paragraphs: 本公司主要的終端市場為水基礎設施的維修與更換，受市府支出與新住宅建設所帶來的新水基礎設施安裝所驅動。因此，本公司業務的相當大一部分取決於地方政府、州政府與聯邦政府在水與污水處理基礎設施升級、維修與更換專案上的支出。水與污水處理基礎設施維修與更換的資金通常來自地方稅收、水費與水價。若州與地方政府或私人水機構在設定稅率、水價與水費時，未能充分預算支出，則可能無法支付水基礎設施的維修與更換費用，尤其在沒有其他資金來源的情況下。此外，與水或污水處理基礎設施相關的聯邦支出減少或延遲，可能會不利於州或地方政府專案，進而可能不利於本公司財務結果。

地方政府與私人水機構可能在增加稅收、水費或水價方面有相當程度的限制。水與污水處理專案被延後與重新排程是常見現象，原因包括專案優先順序的改變、利率上升、通貨膨脹以及難以符合環境及其他政府規範。例如，利率與信貸市場的變化，包括市政債券、房貸、房屋貸款與消費者信貸，過去曾且可能未來會顯著提高本公司產品所應用專案的成本，例如新住宅建設與水與污水處理基礎設施升級、維修與更換專案，並導致這些專案被減少、延後與/或重新排程，進而導致本公司銷售與獲利減少，並不利於財務狀況。此外，較高的利率通常伴隨通貨膨脹。本公司過去曾且可能未來無法足夠提高產品價格以抵銷通貨膨脹速度，這將降低獲利邊際與現金流。
部分州與地方政府可能對其居民的用水施加重大限制，或增加節水措施。這些類型的用水限制與節水措施可能導致私人水機構、市府或其他政府機構的水收入減少，進而可能同樣影響水相關專案的資金決策。
經濟條件不佳可能導致州、市府或私人水機構收到低於預期的收入，進而導致水基礎設施專案的資金減少或延遲。即使經濟條件良好，水基礎設施所有者也可能因種種政治因素或競爭性支出優先順序而選擇不處理延後的基礎設施需求。
水與污水處理基礎設施建設支出低落可能對本公司銷售、獲利與現金流造成不利影響。

新水與污水處理基礎設施支出高度依賴住宅建設。因此，本公司財務表現大幅取決於住宅建設市場的穩定與成長。此市場取決於許多超出本公司控制範疇的因素，包括家庭形成、消費者信心、利率、通貨膨脹與房貸融資的可得性，以及單戶與多戶建設的比例、建設勞動力的可得性，以及最終新建設施是否導致未開發土地的開發。住宅建設市場的不利條件或持續的不確定性已對本公司銷售、獲利與現金流造成不利影響，並可能未來繼續造成不利影響，包括本公司經銷商與/或最終使用客戶決定延後購買或決定不購買本公司產品或服務的風險。
